what: REINFORCE interviewer for Stage 5. Picks the next closed training item from the sequential posterior state; reward is the system's own declared posterior-variance reduction minus a per-question cost (owner RULING 2 -- planted truth never touches the reward, the gradient or any weight).
policy: two-layer MLP, tanh hidden. Input = [theta_hat (8) | per-dimension blur (8) | answered mask (202) | step/horizon (1)] = 219 numbers; output = 202 logits, already-asked items masked to -inf. Seeded init, small output layer so the first policy is nearly uniform.
algorithm: REINFORCE with reward-to-go, a per-step exponential moving-average baseline, advantage normalisation across the batch, and an entropy bonus. Adam, global-norm gradient clipping. Fixed horizon, so the per-question cost is a constant offset on the return and cancels out of the gradient -- it is in the reward because the PRD defines it there.
grading: the trained policy plugs into src.interview.strategies.PolicyStrategy and is graded by src.eval.gate5, the same code as random / fixed / heuristic. It acts greedily at evaluation.

smoke.notes: DEVELOPMENT SANITY ONLY, on the ORIGINAL 400 training personas and their already-drawn Stage 5 sittings. Throwaway: no claim is made from it and it is never graded on the held-out 100.

confirmatory.notes: The Stage 5 confirmatory RL policy. Trains on the 500 fresh RL-batch personas (r0001-r0500, mint seed 549) and their own freshly drawn sittings; the original held-out 100 are refused by src.rl.train.refuse_holdout. Blur reward only.

exploratory_oracle.notes: EXPLORATORY, owner-approved (RULING 2), quarantined. Identical policy and trainer, reward replaced by truth-side squared-error reduction. Trained only by src.eval.rl_oracle, weights named exploratory_oracle, never loadable by a confirmatory code path. Measures the deployable-vs-oracle reward gap.

smoke_discounted.notes: DEVELOPMENT SANITY ONLY. Same as `smoke` but with the discounted return that smoke validation showed is needed; see the `discount` note in this file.

discount_note: SMOKE-VALIDATION FINDING, recorded before the confirmatory run and the reason the discount is 0.9 rather than 1.0. At a fixed horizon with an undiscounted return, the return from every step equals the trace already removed minus the trace left at question N -- the same number whatever ORDER the questions were asked in. So an undiscounted policy is indifferent to ordering: the smoke run learned a good 25-item SET in an arbitrary order, matched the heuristic at N = 25 and tracked RANDOM ordering at N = 5, 10 and 15. Gate 5 is a bar about how few questions are needed, so that objective is misspecified for the task. The per-question cost cannot supply the missing urgency either: at a fixed horizon it is the same constant for every action sequence. Discounting is the standard way to say 'sooner is better' inside a fixed horizon, and it changes the RETURN AGGREGATION, not the reward -- the reward is still the declared posterior-variance reduction minus the per-question cost that owner RULING 2 specifies, and still contains no truth-side term. At gamma = 0.9 the same smoke policy front-loaded after 100 iterations: pooled RMSE 0.798 / 0.707 / 0.673 at N = 5 / 10 / 15 against 0.855 / 0.790 / 0.745 undiscounted, and 0.798 / 0.697 / 0.670 for the info-gain heuristic on the same sitting.
